message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I would not call this ECG normal.** From the image, I see:

- A regular sinus rhythm at roughly **65 beats/minute**.
- Large electrical voltages, suggesting **left ventricular hypertrophy**—possible thickening of the heart’s main pumping chamber.
- **ST-segment and T-wave abnormalities**, including elevation in V1–V3 and depression in lateral leads. These may reflect a hypertrophy “strain” pattern.

That is a provisional interpretation from an image. **It cannot safely exclude a heart attack**, particularly if there are new symptoms; hypertrophy can obscure ischemic changes. [ACC/AHA guidance](https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001029)

**If you currently have chest pain, shortness of breath, sweating, or faintness, call emergency services now.** If you feel well, arrange prompt clinician review, comparison with an older ECG, and consideration of an echocardiogram.

How old is the person, why was this ECG taken, and are there any symptoms or a history of high blood pressure?
